title: Affine model from field generators, with dimension and generic stalk
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension], let $r\ge0$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_r\in E$ satisfy $E=k(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$, meaning that no proper subfield of $E$ contains $k$ and all $e_i$. Put $A=k[e_1,\ldots,e_r]\subseteq E$, the subring of polynomial expressions in these elements with coefficients in $k$, and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $A$ is an integral domain of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and the inclusion $A\subseteq E$ exhibits $E$ as its fraction field: every element of $E$ is $a/b$ for $a,b\in A$ with $b\ne0$. The scheme $U$ is integral and of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its generic point is the zero prime, and the inclusion of $A$ in $E$ induces a $k$-isomorphism $\theta:k(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}E$, where $k(U)$ is the generic stalk [def-sc-function-field]. Its finite topological Krull dimension is $\dim U=\operatorname{trdeg}_k E$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-kun-transcendence-degree]. The surjection $k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to A$, $T_i\mapsto e_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], induces a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbb A^r_k$ over $k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-affine-space].

source.place: Tag 0BXN (theorem-varieties-rational-maps), proof, essential-surjectivity paragraph constructing Spec(A) for a finite-type subalgebra A of the finitely generated field; dimension computation: literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex, Tag 00P0 (lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring).

proof.text: Evaluation $\varepsilon:k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to A$, $T_i\mapsto e_i$, exists by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its image consists of all polynomial expressions in the $e_i$, hence is exactly $A$ by the definition of $A$ in the statement. Thus $\varepsilon$ is surjective, and [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] gives finite type. Since $A\subseteq E$ is a subring containing $1$, one has $0\ne1$ in $A$, and $ab=0$ in $A$ implies $a=0$ or $b=0$ by the field property in $E$. Thus $A$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 0BXN (theorem-varieties-rational-maps), essential-surjectivity paragraph, explicit construction of its finite type subalgebra

proof.text: Inside $E$, put $F=\{a/b:a,b\in A,\ b\ne0\}$. This contains $k$ and each $e_i$, using denominator $1$. It is a subfield: $(a/b)+(c/d)=(ad+bc)/(bd)$, $(a/b)(c/d)=ac/(bd)$, $-(a/b)=(-a)/b$, and a nonzero $a/b$ has inverse $b/a$. The denominators are nonzero since $A$ is a domain; in the inverse formula $a\ne0$. The field-generation hypothesis therefore gives $F=E$. The inclusion is injective and every element of $E$ is such a fraction, exactly the required fraction-field assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BXN (theorem-varieties-rational-maps), essential-surjectivity paragraph, fraction-field assertion expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (2) to the domain $R=A$ with its fraction field $K=E$ from step 2. It gives that $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is integral, that its generic point is $(0)$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,(0)}\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. By [def-sc-function-field] this stalk is $k(U)$. The isomorphism fixes $A$, and hence $k$, so it is the claimed $k$-isomorphism $\theta$. It is induced by the inclusion: on a fraction represented by $a/b$ it must send that fraction to $ab^{-1}$ in $E$, which also makes it unique.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), stalk clause; properties.tex Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral); morphisms.tex Tag 01RW (definition-function-field)

proof.text: The structure map $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: the only nonempty open of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the whole scheme, and its preimage has the single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose coordinate algebra is finite type by step 1. The empty open has the empty affine cover. These are finite covers, as required by the equivalent finite-cover formulation of that definition; [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies the coordinate rings and the map on them.

source.place: Tag 01T0, finite type; definition-finite-type, and the affine-cover characterization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] with the field $k$, the finite type domain $A$ from step 1, and fraction field $E$ from step 2. It says that $\dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_k E$ is finite. Here the fraction field in that statement may be identified with $E$ over $A$; algebraic independence is unchanged under a $k$-isomorphism because polynomial evaluation commutes with it and the isomorphism is injective [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] applied to $R=A$ gives $\dim U=\dim A$, proving the asserted finite topological dimension.

Use the surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism $\varepsilon$ constructed in step 1, and let $h=\operatorname{Spec}\varepsilon:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Take the one-member affine cover of the target by $V=\operatorname{Spec}k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$ itself. Then $h^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, and by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (global sections $A$ and $k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\varepsilon$ induces $\varepsilon$ on them) the map $h^\sharp_V$ is $\varepsilon$, which is surjective. Hence $h$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. By the affine chart formula in [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] for $S=V=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the target is $\mathbb A^r_k$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is over $k$: $\varepsilon$ fixes constants, so the composite $k\to k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A$ is the original coefficient inclusion $k\to A$, and contravariant functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives the commutative triangle over $\operatorname{Spec}k$.
